primary_claim: On Pando, a controlled benchmark of 720+ fine-tuned model organisms with known decision rules and varying rationale faithfulness, gradient-based interpretability methods outperform the blackbox baseline on models trained with no or unfaithful explanations, while non-gradient interpretability methods (SAEs, circuit tracers, logit lens) fail to beat the blackbox baseline despite extensive tuning.

effect.metric: variance in method signal explained by is-field-decision-critical (gradient/RelP vs non-gradient methods)
effect.value: ~56% of RelP signal vs <2.5% of non-gradient methods' signal

contradicts_or_qualifies: Contrasts with AuditBench's free-for-all evaluation stance (e.g. giving a blackbox method a high budget but SAEs only a fixed 50-prompt budget); Pando instead enforces an apples-to-apples comparison with the same fixed input set for every method
stated_future_work: Considering moving to a budget-based prompt system in the future, though designing good prompt-selection strategies for consuming that budget is a current confounder
Welcome further attempts by the community to improve non-gradient method performance on Pando
limitations_stated: Setup is a fairly clean, controlled setup, so negative results should be trusted more than positive results; translating gradient methods' gains to real-world auditing may be harder since decision fields here are very token-aligned
Did not tune logit lens/SAEs/circuit tracers to the specific models, primarily due to cost concerns and for fair comparison, which may better approximate regimes where such tools are undertrained
Pando is intended as a sanity check (if a method can't beat blackbox here, it isn't ready for real-world auditing), not a definitive measure of auditing readiness
quote: Despite our best efforts (e.g. we tested 5+ variants of SAE-based methods and tweaked formatting of the circuit tracer output very hard), we cannot get non-gradient interpretability methods to outperform blackbox methods.
